title: Managed task phase checkpoints and exclusive recovery
outcomes: Resume a bounded active task from its proven phase without stealing a live runner or repeating unconfirmed side effects.

in: Managed native task phase checkpoints, budget resume, ownership/process checks, explicit workspace relocation and side-effect intent/readback interfaces
out: Release publisher implementation, deployment providers and live model topology benchmark
boundaries: Canonical run state, workspace process/integration locks and native phase subprocess

decision_rights: Authorize execution and choose model; GO on 2026-09-13
Implement bounded contract choices and document compatibility behavior

constraints: Opt-in managed native execution uses explicit initial task/workspace/base bindings and frozen model profiles.
Persist intent before a phase/effect and confirmation after it; preserve requirement, context and evidence references.
A process lock plus live parent/worker checks controls recovery; time expiration alone never authorizes a second writer.
Preserve changed code; invalidate affected proof rather than reset files or invent a successful phase.
Local relocation requires explicit identity/path mapping and stopped owners; do not guess another host is idle.
Keep publisher/deployment effects behind explicit intent/readback interfaces for abc-05/06/07.

quality_attributes.scenario: Budget exhausted after build then increased
quality_attributes.measure: Completed build repeated or active task requeued

quality_attributes.scenario: Competing runner or live orphan worker
Crash, code/profile drift or checkout relocation
quality_attributes.measure: Lost requirements/evidence or stale proof treated as passed

quality_attributes.scenario: Interrupted external effect or cleanup failure

risks: Old active tasks without managed checkpoints cannot be assigned a guessed phase; they require explicit recovery context.
